transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. The main reason I’m here is that I'm having a lot of trouble at work lately. I manage health services, and anything that takes real, sitting-down brain work... it just feels like I hit a wall. 

Like, if I have to sit and do my monthly reports or plan a multi-site health event, I just keep putting it off. I know it matters, and I know I need to get it done, but I just avoid it. It's really starting to become a problem.
Have you had trouble focusing and putting off mental tasks like this since you were a child?

Yeah, I have. Even back in elementary school, it was an issue. I remember my teachers telling my parents that I was a bright kid, but I was just always daydreaming. I was constantly losing worksheets, or I'd do my homework and just forget to turn it in. 

It actually got to the point where my mother had to check my backpack every single night just to make sure things got done and handed in. So, yeah, it's been going on for a long time.
Outside of work, does this same kind of trouble with focus and follow-through also cause problems in your day-to-day life?

Yeah, it does. I mean... I’m still getting by, both at work and out in the community. I haven't completely fallen apart. But it definitely causes issues. 

People have had to step in and cover gaps for me when I drop the ball. Deadlines have slipped. It's just... I've really embarrassed myself having to make these last-minute apologies to my friends because I forgot something, and to my coworkers too. So, yeah, it definitely bleeds into my personal life.
Do you have the same trouble with focus and follow-through in more than one setting, such as at home as well as at work?
Yeah, like I was just saying, it's definitely both. It happens at the office, but it's an issue at home, too. So, yes, it's definitely affecting me in more than one setting.
